chunks: And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah

a testimony whose sincerity has been tested, whose essence is our belief; we cling to it forever as long as we live, and store it against the tribulations that befall us, for it is the firm resolve of faith, the opener of goodness, the pleasure of the Merciful, and the defeat of Satan.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the testimony of monotheism in Shia theology according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) presents the Shahada not merely as a verbal utterance but as a 'tested' conviction (mu'taqadan musasan) that serves as the foundational pillar of faith and the key to moral excellence (Ihsan). This declaration is portrayed as a strategic spiritual asset, guarding against the deceptions of Shaytan and securing the pleasure of the Rahman, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the unity of belief, action, and inner sincerity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: I stand witness that there is no god but Allāh the One.

He has no like. My testimony has been tested in its frankness, and its essence is our belief. We shall cling to it for ever till we live and shall store it facing the tribulations that overtake us because it is the foundation stone of Belief (imān) and the first step towards good actions and Divine pleasure. It is the means to keep Satan away.
